reviews.title: Nguyễn Bá Thanh Sơn · IELTS 48 · W09 · Đề 1
reviews.scopeMarkdown:
**Số từ bài gốc: 263 từ**, đếm bằng cách tách nguyên văn theo khoảng trắng. Bài đạt tối thiểu 150 từ nhưng vượt khung 150–200 từ của lớp.
Phạm vi: Cô chấm Đề 1 đã gõ; chưa chấm Đề 2 hoặc bản scan.
reviews.overall: Em cần sửa và nộp lại. Bài dài 263 từ, trong khi Overview gộp France và Belgium vào xu hướng trái ngược chưa đúng. Bài này em làm còn ẩu ở việc kiểm tra chủ thể: “France … rose” và “Belgium remained” tiếp tục dùng tên nước để mô tả tỷ lệ phần trăm. Em đã vận dụng cách đưa số liệu lên đầu, “with a subsequent…” và quy chiếu cho Italy, nhưng cần dùng nhất quán khi chuyển nước. Đây là kiến thức em đã ghi chép và Cô đã giảng kỹ; em cần hiểu và vận dụng lại để tự sửa, đồng thời chọn mốc gọn hơn.
reviews.dataGrouping: Detail 1 trình bày Germany đến cuối kỳ, rồi Italy và France đến năm 2008; Detail 2 tiếp tục Italy, thêm United Kingdom, trở lại France và kết thúc bằng Belgium. Đây là cách triển khai có đan xen thời gian và quốc gia, chưa phải hai nửa thời gian tách biệt. Cô giữ các nước và thứ tự trong hai Detail của em, rút các mốc trung gian theo C06; trong bản gợi ý, Cô dùng cụm mở đoạn bao quát các diễn biến còn lại theo C08.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line graph illustrates the percentages of female members of parliament in five European countries, namely Germany, Italy, France, the UK and Belgium, over a period of 12 years, commencing from 2000 to 2012.
Overall, there was a general increase in the percentage of female members of parliament in Germany, Italy and the UK, while an opposite trend was observed in the case of France and Belgium towards the end of the period. Also of note is that Germany consistently had one of the highest figures throughout the years, whereas the UK started with the lowest percentage but experienced the most significant growth.
To elaborate, in 2000, around 33% of parliament members in Germany were female, with a subsequent gradual rise to approximately 35% in 2004 and 2008, before reaching 37% in 2012. The figure for Italy, meanwhile, increased steadily from about 26% in 2000 to 30% in 2004 and 33% in 2008. France, conversely, rose sharply from 25% to approximately 37% in 2004, before falling to around 29% in 2008.
Regarding the latter half of the provided timeline, the percentage of female parliament members in Italy continued to increase, but to a far greater extent, reaching approximately 39% in 2012, marking the highest point of the entire chart. A growth was likewise recorded in the figure for the UK, which rose dramatically from only 3% in 2000 to 20% in 2008 and then 28% in 2012. Finally, France recovered slightly to around 32% in 2012, while Belgium remained relatively stable at approximately 28–29% after its initial rise from 17% in 2000.

The given pie charts illustrate the main reasons why students chose a particular university in the UK in 1997 and 2007.
Overall, there was a general increase in the proportions of students choosing a university because of suitable degree courses and proximity to their parental home, while an opposite trend was observed in the case of quality of resources, quality of teaching and good sports and social activities. Also of note is that suitable degree courses consistently had the highest figure in both years, whereas good sports and social activities experienced the most significant decline.
To elaborate, in 1997, around 35% of students chose a particular university because of its suitable degree courses, with a subsequent slight rise to 37% in 2007. The figure for quality of resources, conversely, fell from 21% to 17% during the same period. Meanwhile, proximity to parental home increased considerably, from only 10% in 1997 to 22% in 2007, becoming the second most common reason in the latter year.
Regarding the latter half of the provided timeline, the proportion of students choosing a university because of quality of teaching increased slightly from 15% in 1997 to 18% in 2007. A decline was likewise recorded in the figure for good sports and social activities, falling from 19% to only 6%, which represented the largest decrease among all the categories. Finally, although suitable degree courses remained the most important reason in both years, its figure changed only slightly, while the other reasons showed more noticeable changes over the period.
